nameStory: River Thyme Moss gets its name from its preferred habitat along rocky streams and riverbanks, where it forms dense, cushiony mats. The 'thyme' part comes from its tiny, overlapping leaves that somewhat resemble the herb thyme when viewed up close, though the two plants are completely unrelated.
description: River Thyme Moss is a small but distinctive moss that forms compact, bright green cushions along stream edges and wet rocks. Individual plants are tiny, rarely more than an inch tall, but they cluster together to create dense mats that can cover several square feet. When dry, the cushions turn yellowish-green and feel firm to the touch, but they quickly plump up and brighten when moistened. This moss produces reddish-brown capsules on slender stalks that arch gracefully over the leafy cushions.

idTips.label: Growth Form
idTips.description: Forms dense, compact cushions that feel springy underfoot when wet but firm and crunchy when dry

idTips.label: Habitat
idTips.description: Always found on wet rocks or soil right at water's edge - if it's not near flowing water, it's probably not River Thyme Moss

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Tiny, oval leaves overlap like shingles, creating a smooth texture that feels almost velvety when stroked gently

idTips.label: Color
idTips.description: Bright emerald green when wet, fading to yellowish or brownish-green when dry - the color change is dramatic

idTips.label: Sporophytes
idTips.description: Reddish-brown capsules on curved stalks appear in late spring, looking like tiny street lamps bending over the moss cushions

habitat: River Thyme Moss is found exclusively along the edges of clean, fast-moving streams and rivers throughout New England's mountainous regions. It grows on constantly moist rocks, fallen logs, and mineral-rich soil within the splash zone of flowing water. You'll most often spot it in shaded ravines and gorges where the humidity stays high year-round.

seasonality.spring: Bright green cushions are most vibrant as snowmelt feeds streams. Sporophyte capsules begin developing on curved stalks, appearing as small brown bumps.
seasonality.summer: Maintains steady green color in consistently moist spots, though exposed areas may brown during dry spells. Mature capsules release spores and gradually wither.
seasonality.fall: Cushions often show their most dramatic colors, from deep green in wet areas to golden-brown where water levels have dropped.
seasonality.winter: Remains visible under snow and ice, often the only green plant visible along frozen stream edges. Growth slows but doesn't stop completely.

funFact: River Thyme Moss can absorb up to 20 times its dry weight in water and will visibly transform from a crunchy brown mat to a lush green carpet in less than 30 seconds when splashed by stream water.
confusionNotes: Often confused with other streamside mosses, but River Thyme Moss's exclusive habitat right at the water's edge is the key - remember 'thyme by the stream' and you'll look in the right spot every time.
contextualKnowledge: Despite its name suggesting a connection to the culinary herb thyme, this moss is completely unrelated to any flowering plants. The name similarity is purely based on the visual resemblance of their small, overlapping leaves.
compareHints: River Thyme Moss is the only species in its genus found in New England, making it unique among our regional mosses. It's most similar to other cushion-forming mosses in the Mniaceae family, but differs by its exclusive streamside habitat and dramatic color changes with moisture levels. While other cushion mosses might occasionally grow near water, none are as strictly aquatic in their requirements.
